headline: Q1: Streaming reliability + enterprise auth hardening land in parallel; tool-calling pipeline hardening queued for Q2
body:
Two Q1 workstreams are landing concurrently, both scoped at effort 8 with no cross-dependencies, so they can proceed in parallel tracks.

Streaming: we're fixing a cluster of provider/abstraction-specific bugs rather than one root cause. Key items: tolerate SSE payloads missing the 'event:' field (hits Anthropic-via-Bedrock-proxy, currently a hard failure with zero generation chunks); stop with_structured_output streaming from emitting spurious Pydantic serializer warnings and dropping response metadata/headers like x-request-id; fix disable_streaming='tool_calling' which currently throws an AttributeError (AsyncStream passed where a ChatCompletion is expected) and, even when it doesn't crash, disables streaming globally instead of scoping to tool-calling turns only; and route agent/graph internal LLM calls through astream instead of ainvoke so on_llm_new_token actually fires when graph-level streaming (use_astream=True) is enabled — today it silently falls back to batched output. Supporting work includes closing test-coverage gaps and release sequencing for tool-call streaming across integration packages (relevant for providers like Mistral), plus fixing a known-incorrect assertion in the core streaming error-callback test suite that currently masks whether error-path behavior for empty streamed generations is correct. Watch for behavioral-change risk on the disable_streaming fix — it changes existing (buggy) global-disable semantics to turn-scoped, which could break code depending on the current behavior. The SSE tolerance fix for missing 'event:' fields also risks masking genuinely malformed responses from other providers.

Authentication: ChatAnthropic (and similar integrations) gets support for custom HTTP clients with mTLS, unblocking cert-based/PKI auth behind corporate proxies. MCP tool discovery gets fixed so configured auth headers/tokens are reliably forwarded during tool discovery instead of causing spurious 403s. We're also introducing a shared httpx client/connection-pooling layer intended to unify AzureChatOpenAI and BaseChatOpenAI (currently redundant, inconsistent setups), with at least two provider integrations migrating in this cycle. Separately, SSRF/allowlist host validation is being hardened to close a bypass via environment-based auth checks — flagged high-risk since it could break legitimate enterprise configs that currently rely on env-based checks to reach internal hosts, so this needs careful scoping.

Tool-calling pipeline work (Gemini thought-signature/turn-order validation for injected tool-call history, malformed/fragmented streamed tool-call payload handling, tool_choice defaults breaking reasoning models forced into 'required', HITL rejection enforcement gaps in ToolNode, missing tool_call_id on on_tool_start/on_tool_end, reactive-only tool-call limit enforcement, and inconsistent ToolException/handle_tool_error behavior across @tool vs ToolNode) is scheduled for Q2, same effort level, no stated dependency on the Q1 items.
call_to_action: Review the disable_streaming='tool_calling' scoping change and the astream-routing change for agent/graph paths for sequencing conflicts with your own in-flight work, and flag if the shared httpx client refactor touches auth flows you own in AzureChatOpenAI/BaseChatOpenAI before it merges.
